_comment: Canonical capability/backend vocabulary for the Lego matcher. A template's capabilities.json (provides/requires) MAY ONLY use capability and backend tokens defined here. Anything outside this set must be emitted with "confidence": "review" so a human canonicalises it later — it must NEVER be invented silently, or the deterministic matcher wires incompatible components. 'capability' is the service class a consumer requires and a provider offers; 'backend' is the concrete implementation (postgresql vs mysql). Two things are compatible only when the capability matches AND the consumer's accepted backends intersect the provider's backend. 'connection_fields' are the canonical FIELD ROLES a wiring carries — the batch maps each to the real (often prefixed) schema field, e.g. role 'host' -> schema field 'db_host'. Grounded in configs/package_catalog.json categories, but split finer where the catalog is too coarse for correct wiring (redis/memcached are catalog-category 'database' but are 'cache' here, so a cache consumer is never wired to PostgreSQL).

database.description: A relational / document data store a client connects to over the network to read and write application data.
database.notes: sqlite is file-embedded and has no host/port — a 'sqlite' backend never participates in network wiring. mariadb and mysql are wire-compatible: a consumer accepting 'mysql' also accepts 'mariadb'.

cache.description: An in-memory key/value cache or store used to offload a database or share ephemeral state.
cache.notes: valkey and keydb are redis-protocol drop-ins: a consumer accepting 'redis' also accepts them.

message_queue.description: A broker for asynchronous messages / events between services.
message_queue.notes: mqtt is the protocol; mosquitto is a common mqtt broker (backend 'mqtt'). redis appears here too (pub/sub) — a queue consumer accepting 'redis' means it uses redis as a broker, distinct from the 'cache' capability.

web_server.description: An HTTP origin server that serves static files or hosts an application, sitting BEHIND a reverse proxy or directly exposed.
web_server.notes: Distinct from reverse_proxy: this is the thing being proxied TO.

reverse_proxy.description: An HTTP(S) reverse proxy / load balancer that terminates client connections and forwards to upstream web_server or app_runtime backends.
reverse_proxy.notes: Several servers can be both web_server and reverse_proxy (nginx, caddy, apache) — the template declares whichever role its config expresses.

app_runtime.description: An application process a web server forwards dynamic requests to over FastCGI/uWSGI/HTTP.
app_runtime.notes: php-fpm typically provides a unix socket (role 'socket'); a web_server requires it as an upstream.

dns_authoritative.description: An authoritative DNS server answering for zones it owns.

dns_resolver.description: A recursive/forwarding DNS resolver clients point resolv.conf at.

mail_smtp.description: An SMTP server that accepts/relays outgoing mail — what an application uses to send email.

mail_imap.description: An IMAP/POP3 server that stores and serves user mailboxes.

directory.description: An LDAP directory / identity source clients bind to for users and groups.

nfs.description: An NFS export server; clients mount an exported path. Wiring INJECTS the client address into the server's exports list (peer_injection).

smb.description: An SMB/CIFS file server; clients mount shares.

ntp.description: A time source clients synchronise their clock to.

container_runtime.description: A container engine that runs images (as an orchestration target or a Docker-API endpoint).

ssh.description: An SSH server clients connect to for shell/SFTP/tunnels.

log_sink.description: A syslog/log collector that other hosts forward their logs to.

metrics_sink.description: A metrics store/collector that agents push to or that scrapes exporters.

search.description: A full-text search / analytics engine clients index into and query.

backend_aliases._comment: Wire-compatible substitutes: if a consumer accepts the key, it also accepts the values. The matcher expands these before intersecting.
